newsitem.title: ITALY: Enron, Enel to sign joint venture - source.
newsitem.headline: Enron, Enel to sign joint venture - source.

text.p: U.S. company Enron Corp will sign a letter of intent with Italian utility giant L'Ente Nazionale per L'Energia Elettrica (Enel) to create a major generating force on the Italian market, an industrial source said on Tuesday.

Enel will contribute a maximum 5,000 megawatts of existing electricity generating capacity worth an estimated five trillion lire to the 50-50 joint venture, the source said. An official announcement was due later on Tuesday.

Enel was also expected to transfer around $2.4 billion of debts to the venture, but full details of the deal have yet to be finalised, the source said. Houston-based Enron is one of the world's largest natural gas and electricity companies.
Enel announced a similar joint venture earlier this year with Italian energy group Eni, as it prepares for the 1999 liberalisation of the Italian electricity market.

Under current regulations, Enel enjoys a virtual monoploy over generation and distribution but under the terms of the planned liberalisation, up to 30 percent of the domestic market will be opened up to competition.
Enel, which has total generating capacity of around 55,000 Megawatts, expects that its joint ventures will compete in the open market.
